output.summary: The yield drop is real: customer PPM rose and the CMM measurement system was stable. The new-operator cohort is ruled out, because their reject rate matches experienced operators and yield fell before they ran alone. Three causes are confounded and untested: Corvane bar hardness scatter, a spindle service deferred since May (runout rising, worst on L3-02 and L3-05), and 12-hour shifts. Scrap-tag times are an artifact of batch writing, so the fatigue evidence is weak. The tighter tolerance on the long-shaft machines confounds the machine-level comparison. The Line 6 Corvane results and the staggered service-and-trial design (A2) can separate the causes. Reverting shifts, blaming steel, punishing operators or cutting inspection is not justified now.
